A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeTok and SETOKIM under the same title and authorship. All 20 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v3, including Appendices A-E, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables and rendered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original SETOKIM benchmark results, clustering comparisons, component ablations, transfer experiments and qualitative outputs in the main text and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 reports original tokenizer reconstruction/classification results, SETOKIM benchmark results, component and encoder-freezing ablations, connector comparisons and qualitative demonstrations.

M1.justification: v3 adds inter-cluster Transformers and concept-level contrastive training, replaces v1's Q-former/Stable Diffusion reconstruction pipeline with a Transformer-based detokenizer, and uses a diffusion loss for visual next-token generation instead of embedding MSE. Appendix C also changes cluster assignment through a sigmoid and seed-score penalty. These change the proposed procedure beyond renaming the cluster and merger.

E1.justification: v3 adds ImageNet reconstruction/classification evaluation and explicit in-context and multi-image reasoning demonstrations. MA5K replaces Emu-Edit, while NoCaps, VSR, IconQA, VizWiz, TextQA and MMBench evaluations disappear. Training coverage also changes substantially, including ImageNet/OpenImages tokenizer supervision and SlimPajama text training. POPE, MME and MM-Vet are retained from v1's separate benchmark table.

E2.justification: v3 adds NExT-GPT, CM3Leon and Chameleon to understanding comparisons; ReLA and SEEM enter quantitative segmentation comparisons while GLaMM and MiniGPT-v2 leave them. LaVIT and Morph-Token enter generation/editing comparisons. Table 3 introduces a separate tokenizer comparator suite, and Appendix E adds MLP and Q-former connector controls alongside the retained Resampler comparison.

E3.justification: The reported configurations change from Vicuna-v1.5 at 7B/13B with ViT-G/14-336 or ConvNext-XXL to LLaMA-2-7B with SigLIP at 384 resolution. Training tables revise learning rates, weight decay, warmup and per-GPU batch size. New evaluations introduce ImageNet rFID/Top-1 and MA5K LPIPS. These settings prevent treating the revised benchmark scores as matched-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: v1's positional-encoding and merger ablations are retained but expanded in v3 Table 6 to contrastive loss and inner/inter-cluster Transformers across reconstruction, understanding and generation. v3 adds encoder-freezing and controlled connector studies. Conversely, v1's threshold-clustering analysis, CNN-versus-ViT analysis and small-data retrofit experiments on Emu, LLaVA and Yi-VL are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run uncertainty. v1's feature-score distribution plot concerns clustering behavior rather than uncertainty in reported model performance; average token counts likewise do not constitute repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. For example, the reported 7B VQAv2/GQA scores change from 79.6/64.4 in v1 Table 1 to 78.7/65.6 in v3 Table 1, under changed configurations. v3 newly reports ImageNet rFID 2.07 and Top-1 accuracy 76.4, alongside revised segmentation, editing and ablation results. These are revised-system outcomes, not isolated performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 adds the formal concept-level contrastive objective in Appendix C.2, substitutes kernel values for Euclidean distances in the density/distance definitions, and revises Algorithm 1's seed selection and mask updates. These are substantive mathematical changes, although neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The two purported contrastive directions in v3 Equations 5-6 are algebraically identical as printed.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of dynamic, semantically complete visual tokens and a generalist MLLM covering understanding, generation, segmentation and editing. v3's introduction and conclusion revise the contribution description to emphasize explicit contrastive alignment and unified autoregressive training, while dropping v1's introductory claim of easy integration into established MLLMs with minimal adaptation.

C2.justification: v3 develops new explanations connecting reconstruction-only training to insufficient semantic learning, encoder unfreezing to recovery of low-level detail, and concept tokens to editing operations. v1's explanations of threshold generalization and CNN receptive-field limitations disappear with those analyses. Appendix B also revises applicability limits from 7B/13B and 336 resolution to 7B and 384 resolution.

D1.justification: v3 substantially revises implementation and training documentation: Transformer depths, token dimensions, detokenizer and diffusion-MLP construction, fuller dataset sizes, bfloat16 precision and gradient accumulation are specified. Reported hardware changes from 16 A800 GPUs to 16 H100 GPUs, and training recipes are replaced. Some earlier details, including the one-epoch entries, disappear; the project-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands methodological positioning around TiTok, GroupViT and autoregressive generation with diffusion loss, and compares against newer systems including Morph-Token and Chameleon. Its tokenizer-quality discussion explicitly contrasts spatial grids and fixed one-dimensional latents with SeTok. The existing scene-decomposition discussion and first-solution novelty claim largely remain; citation-style changes alone are not counted.

P1.justification: The methodology, introductory contribution narrative and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. v3 introduces a separate Settings section, promotes expanded ablations into the main text and reorganizes the method appendix. Separating tokenizer training from SETOKIM's two stages replaces v1's unified three-stage presentation; that regrouping alone does not establish removal of a training stage.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the introductory tokenizer comparison and provides separate SeTok and SETOKIM architecture diagrams. It consolidates understanding tables, restructures generation/editing tables with representation and decoder columns, and adds tokenizer-quality and expanded ablation displays. Token-mask and reconstruction examples change, and new generation, captioning and multi-image panels appear. Several earlier qualitative panels are retained with renumbering and edits.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the empirical argument with direct tokenizer evaluation, broader component ablations and comparisons controlling the encoder and training data. However, its new central contrastive objective is not unambiguously specified: Appendix C.2 prints identical expressions for the two claimed directions. MagicBrush is also newly listed as training data while Table 2 retains a zero-shot editing label. The PDFs do not resolve whether these reflect presentation errors or experimental differences. These methodological and reporting uncertainties prevent reliably weighing the added validation against its limitations.
